title: Esther 2
paragraphs: ¹ Sometime later, when King Ahasuerus had calmed down, he thought about Vashti — what she had done and what had been decreed against her. ² His personal attendants suggested, "Let a search be made for beautiful young virgins for the king. ³ Let the king appoint commissioners in every province of his kingdom to bring all these beautiful young women to the harem in Shushan the palace, under the care of Hegai the king's eunuch, who is in charge of the women. Let them be given their beauty treatments. ⁴ Then let the young woman who pleases the king become queen in Vashti's place." The king liked this idea and acted on it. ⁵ Now there was in Shushan the palace a Jew named Mordecai, the son of Jair, son of Shimei, son of Kish, a Benjamite,

⁶ who had been carried into exile from Jerusalem along with the captives taken with Jeconiah king of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had deported. ⁷ Mordecai had raised his cousin Hadassah — that is, Esther — because she had no father or mother. The girl was lovely and beautiful, and when her parents died, Mordecai had taken her as his own daughter. ⁸ When the king's decree was proclaimed and many young women were brought to Shushan the palace under Hegai's care, Esther was among those brought to the palace. ⁹ Hegai was pleased with her and showed her favor, quickly providing her with her beauty treatments and her special food, along with seven maids chosen from the palace, and moving her and her maids into the best rooms in the harem. ¹⁰ Esther had not revealed her nationality or family background, because Mordecai had instructed her to keep it secret.

¹¹ Every day Mordecai walked back and forth near the courtyard of the harem to learn how Esther was faring and what was happening to her. ¹² Before a young woman's turn came to go in to King Ahasuerus, she had to complete twelve months of beauty treatments — six months with oil of myrrh and six months with perfumes and cosmetics, as was the custom. ¹³ When a girl's turn came, she could take with her whatever she wanted from the harem to the king's palace. ¹⁴ She would go in the evening, and the next morning she would return to a second harem under the care of Shaashgaz, the king's eunuch who kept the concubines. She would not see the king again unless he was particularly pleased with her and summoned her by name. ¹⁵ When it was Esther's turn — the daughter of Abihail, the uncle of Mordecai who had adopted her — she asked for nothing beyond what Hegai the king's eunuch advised. And everyone who saw her was captivated by her.

¹⁶ Esther was brought to King Ahasuerus in his royal palace in the tenth month — the month of Tebeth — in the seventh year of his reign. ¹⁷ The king loved Esther more than all the other women, and she won his grace and favor more than any of the other virgins. He placed the royal crown on her head and made her queen in Vashti's place. ¹⁸ The king gave a great banquet in Esther's honor — Esther's feast — for all his officials and servants, and he proclaimed a public holiday throughout the provinces and distributed gifts with royal generosity. ¹⁹ When the virgins were assembled a second time, Mordecai was sitting at the king's gate. ²⁰ Esther still had not revealed her family background or nationality, just as Mordecai had instructed her — she continued to follow his directions as she had when he was bringing her up.

²¹ During this time, while Mordecai was sitting at the king's gate, two of the king's eunuchs — Bigthan and Teresh, who guarded the doorway — became furious and plotted to assassinate King Ahasuerus. ²² But Mordecai learned of the plot and reported it to Queen Esther, who told the king in Mordecai's name. ²³ When the matter was investigated and confirmed, both men were hanged on a gallows. All of this was recorded in the book of the chronicles in the king's presence.
